title: Uber and Ola: post-deactivation worker challenge and judicial explanation orders

observations.claim: The Amsterdam appellate record addresses automated fraud-related decisions and account removal affecting drivers.
limits: Bounded to the cited public record and instrument posture.

observations.claim: The public court release states that drivers were not heard before the decisions.
limits: Bounded to the cited public record and instrument posture.

observations.claim: The court required factors, reasons and information needed to understand and contest the automated decisions.
limits: Bounded to the cited public record and instrument posture.

observations.claim: The recovered counterpower actors are the affected workers and an external court rather than an internal predeployment representative body.
limits: Bounded to the cited public record and instrument posture.

observations.claim: The order makes evidence and explanation more addressable but does not itself recover full reinstatement, pay restoration or record repair.
limits: Bounded to the cited public record and instrument posture.

observations.claim: No public record in this lane shows that an upheld challenge changed the fraud model, threshold, workflow or validation population.
limits: Bounded to the cited public record and instrument posture.

findings.claim: Judicial review can create real post-harm counterpower by compelling information that the platform did not supply voluntarily.
limits: No unpublished term, universal prevalence, named-company intent, or complete worker outcome is inferred.

findings.claim: Explanation after account removal is later and narrower than collective participation before the model and threshold are fixed.
limits: No unpublished term, universal prevalence, named-company intent, or complete worker outcome is inferred.

findings.claim: Evidence access is not equivalent to restoration, and restoration is not equivalent to system correction.
limits: No unpublished term, universal prevalence, named-company intent, or complete worker outcome is inferred.

findings.claim: Preaction support, collective pattern access, full worker outcomes and model revision remain blocked.
limits: No unpublished term, universal prevalence, named-company intent, or complete worker outcome is inferred.
